# Company Income Tax in Nigeria: A Practical Guide to Business Tax Obligations


- Oluwakemi Adesina


- September 27, 2026


Table of Contents


Toggle


A business can be profitable on paper and still struggle to pay salaries if too much cash is tied up in unpaid invoices, inventory, or other commitments.


That is one reason company income tax in Nigeria deserves more attention than simply calculating a percentage at the end of the year. Your tax position depends on how your business is structured, what it earns, which expenses are recognised for tax purposes, the records supporting those expenses, and the rules that apply to your company.


For businesses operating in Nigeria, the framework changed significantly with the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which took effect from 1 January 2026 alongside the new tax administration framework.


This guide explains how Company Income Tax (CIT) works under the current framework, who it applies to, how taxable profit is determined, what records your business should keep, and where financial management fits into the process.


##


**What is Company Income Tax in Nigeria?**


Company Income Tax (CIT) is a tax imposed on the taxable profits of companies under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.


The important word is profits.


CIT is not simply a percentage of every naira that enters your business account. Your business may record ₦80 million in turnover without having ₦80 million of taxable profit.


The tax calculation starts with the company’s financial results and applies the adjustments required by tax law to arrive at the amount on which tax is assessed.


This distinction matters because turnover, accounting profit and taxable profit are not necessarily the same number.


###


**Company Income Tax vs Personal Income Tax**


CIT applies to companies, while Personal Income Tax generally applies to individuals.


For example, if you operate through an incorporated company, the company’s tax obligations are separate from your personal income tax obligations. Paying yourself a salary or receiving other personal income can create separate tax considerations.


The[structure of the business](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/) therefore matters before you even get to the calculation.


##


**Which Businesses are subject to Company Income Tax?**


Your company tax obligations can depend on factors such as turnover, fixed assets, residency, sector, and whether the business qualifies for a specific incentive or special tax regime.


Small businesses are the ones with gross turnover of not more than ₦50 million per year and total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250 million, subject to the conditions in the Act. Small businesses are taxed at 0% under the Act.


For businesses that do not fall within the small-business definition, the general company income tax rate under the Act is **30%** .


##


**How is Company Income Tax in Nigeria Calculated?**


The starting point is your company’s financial result, but the amount eventually subject to tax is determined under the tax rules.


A simple way to understand the process is:


**Revenue → accounting profit → tax adjustments → taxable profit → applicable taxes and levies**


Accounting profit is the profit reported in your financial statements after accounting for your income and expenses.


Taxable profit in Nigeria is the amount arrived at after applying the adjustments required by tax law.


That means an expense appearing in your profit and loss statement does not automatically mean that the same amount will reduce your taxable profit.


Some expenses may receive different treatment for tax purposes, while qualifying capital expenditure may be dealt with through capital allowance rules rather than simply deducted as an ordinary operating expense.


##


**Which Business Expenses Can Reduce Taxable Profit?**


Tax treatment depends on the rules applicable to the particular expense.


For example, ordinary business costs such as staff costs, rent, utilities, supplies and other operating expenses may form part of the company’s deductible expenditure where they satisfy the relevant requirements.


Capital expenditure is different. Buying a vehicle, production equipment or other long-term business assets should not automatically be treated in the same way as paying an electricity bill or buying office supplies.


##


**Why Your Financial Records Matter for Tax**


Tax compliance is much easier when your[financial records](https://www.ifrs.org/) can answer basic questions quickly.


Where did the revenue come from?


What did the business spend?


Who was paid?


Why was the expense incurred?


What document supports the transaction?


Which expenses relate to the business?


Which assets does the company own?


For business tax compliance in Nigeria, these are the records to keep:


1. Sales invoices and receipts
2. Supplier invoices and supporting documents
3. Bank statements
4. Payroll records
5. Expense records
6. Asset registers
7. Contracts and relevant agreements
8. Records supporting business-related payments


Good documentation gives your finance team a reliable picture of how the business is actually performing.


###


**Keep Business and Personal Money Separate**


Using the company’s bank account to pay personal bills may cause the business to have a long list of transactions that require explanation and reconciliation.


That creates unnecessary work for the finance team and makes it harder to distinguish genuine business expenditure from personal transactions.


Separate business and personal finances from the beginning. It is much easier to maintain clean records than to reconstruct them months later.


##


**Company Income Tax Filing and Compliance**


Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a company that has been in business for more than 18 months generally has up to six months after the end of its accounting year to file its return. The Act also specifies[the documents and information](https://nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11249) that accompany company returns, including the relevant financial statements and tax computations, with specific treatment for small businesses.


The exact filing requirements can vary according to the company’s circumstances, so businesses should check the current requirements of the Nigeria Revenue Service before filing.


The former Federal Inland Revenue Service has also been replaced within the new institutional framework by the[Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS)](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/) , which now administers the relevant federal tax system.


##


**Common Company Income Tax Mistakes Businesses make**


###


**1. Treating turnover as profit**


Turnover tells you how much business came in. Profit tells you what remains after relevant costs. Tax calculations introduce another layer by applying the rules that determine taxable profit.


###


**2. Assuming every expense is tax-deductible**


An expense can be genuine and still receive a different treatment for tax purposes.


###


**3. Treating depreciation as a normal tax deduction**


Accounting depreciation and tax treatment are not interchangeable. Capital assets may be dealt with through capital allowances under the tax rules.


###


**4. Mixing personal and business transactions**


When personal spending sits inside the company’s books, reconciling company tax obligations becomes harder and the business’s financial picture becomes less reliable.


###


**5. Leaving records until tax season**


Monthly bookkeeping gives the business a much earlier view of revenue, expenses, cash position and potential tax obligations.


###


**6. Using outdated tax information**


Nigeria’s tax framework changed substantially from January 2026.


##


**How Better Financial Management Makes Tax Compliance Easier**


Tax compliance starts long before the tax return.


If your business records every transaction properly, reconciles its accounts regularly and keeps supporting documents, the eventual tax computation becomes a structured process rather than a frantic exercise in finding missing information.


A useful monthly routine can include:


1. Reconcile business bank accounts.
2. Record and categorise business income and expenses.
3. Review outstanding customer invoices.
4. Check supplier and expense documentation.
5. Update payroll records.
6. Review major purchases and capital assets separately.
7. Review the monthly profit and loss statement.
8. Flag unusual or unclear transactions for your accountant or tax adviser.


This creates another benefit that has little to do with tax.


You also start seeing the business more clearly.

##


**Conclusion**


Company income tax is easier to manage when it is treated as part of the business’s financial system.


Know your turnover. Know your actual costs. Keep supporting documents. Separate business and personal spending. Review your accounts regularly. And before relying on a tax rate or threshold, make sure it belongs to the tax year you are actually filing for.

##


**Frequently Asked Questions**


###


**What is Company Income Tax in Nigeria?**


Company Income Tax is a tax on the taxable profits of companies under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.


###


**What is the current CIT rate in Nigeria?**


Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, small companies are taxed at 0%, while companies outside the small-company category are subject to a 30% company income tax rate.


###


**Do small companies pay Company Income Tax?**


Small companies are subject to a 0% CIT rate under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. They should not, however, assume that a 0% CIT rate means they have no tax or filing obligations at all. Other taxes and compliance requirements may still apply depending on the company’s circumstances.


###


**Is Company Income Tax calculated on turnover?**


No. CIT is based on taxable profits rather than simply applying the tax rate to total turnover.


###


**Is accounting profit the same as taxable profit?**


No. Accounting profit is determined under financial reporting rules, while taxable profit is determined after applying the relevant tax rules and adjustments.


###


**Can business expenses reduce taxable profit?**


Some business expenses may be deductible where they satisfy the requirements of the tax law. Other expenses may be treated differently, particularly capital expenditure. Proper documentation is important in supporting the treatment of expenses.


###


**Does payroll affect a company’s tax position?**


Payroll is an important business cost and needs to be properly recorded. The tax treatment of employee-related costs depends on the applicable tax rules and the circumstances of the expenditure.


###


**When should a company file its tax return?**


Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, companies that have been in business for more than 18 months generally file within six months after the end of their accounting year. Specific circumstances can affect filing requirements, so companies should confirm the current requirements applicable to them.


###


**Has FIRS been replaced?**


The new tax administration framework established the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), which now serves as the federal tax administration body within the reformed system.
